staticEvidence.independentUnit: JVM fork; measurement windows are nested

dynamicValidation.findings: Dynamic validation completed 42 independent JVM forks across 7 fixtures (R7, R15, R23 gate/body returns and R15 scarcity return) with 1008 nested 5s windows. While qualifying recovery (within 5% of tail mean for 2 consecutive windows) occurred rapidly in <= 10s (window 2) for 13 of 14 transitions, substantial inter-fork variance and persistent throughput deficits vs POLICY_OFF were observed. Specifically: (1) R7-gate-return in plentiful phase showed fork 0 at -21.92% vs OFF, with mean steady delta of -5.83% and transient drops to -22.99%; (2) R23-gate-return returning to scarce exhibited severe deficits in two forks (-31.75% and -41.95% vs OFF), with return-vs-initial throughputs showing wide spread across forks; (3) R7-body-return and R15-body-return returning to low body exhibited stark fork bifurcation (e.g. R7 fork 1 at -21.86% vs fork 2 at +34.09%; R15 fork 2 at -23.97% and -23.91% return vs initial); (4) R15 scarcity return fork 1 showed a -24.96% steady deficit in less-scarce phase and -17.23% in return-to-scarce phase. Conversely, the policy demonstrated strong protection against OFF collapse under R23 plentiful gate conditions (+312.87% and +80.51%) and solid body benefits on R23 (+39.68% steady mean). Because throughput-only measurements cannot establish underlying mechanisms (such as gate exit hysteresis, owner-local productive-handle refresh, or contention half-life decay) and fork-level deficits remain significant, the policy is marked NEEDS FOLLOW-UP without altering coefficients or production defaults.
